::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 10 [1894?]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

Dear Madam
I send two of the books you wish for. [The Cross Roads](cmy_books/cmybook_221.qmd) is I find being read to a class of [G F S](organizations/other_23.qmd) girls, but will be finished by the time you have done with these two. [John Brent](other_books/otherbook_211.qmd) is by S Baring Gould, one of the penny SPCK series. I know I have it and have read it aloud, but I cannot lay my hand on it this moment.

I have only one copy of the [Chimes](cmy_books/cmybook_232.qmd), which is being read every week so I cannot well send it. Our Mothers are fairly punctual, and the accounts cover the little irregular time so we begin with the Litany provided by the [Mother’s Union](organizations/other_31.qmd) and then have the religious reading. It is a better time for the [Vicar](people/person_184.qmd)’s being able to come as he does sometimes that[sic] at the end, when the children are apt to get restless

Yours truly
C M Yonge		

There is a <u>very</u> good SPCK tract called ‘The Black Copse’[^1]

---

[^1]: Not found.
